blocks.en: 📖 Evangelism — Unit 8: Evangelistic Preaching
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Evangelismo — Unidad 8: Predicación Evangelística

blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary · Dr. Wayne Cook, Author and Professor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Seminary Director
blocks.es_reference: Seminario Teológico de Chapala · Dr. Wayne Cook, Autor y Profesor · Dr. Ted Rogers, Director del Seminario

blocks.en: Orientation: Preaching at Its Best
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: La Predicación en Su Mejor Forma

blocks.en: Personal evangelism is the most common form of gospel proclamation, but it is not the only form. From Peter at Pentecost to Whitefield in the fields and Spurgeon in the Tabernacle, God has used public proclamation to gather thousands. Faris Whitesell put it sharply: "Evangelistic preaching is preaching at its best. It is preaching adapted to the highest ends of the gospel — turning men from sin and darkness to salvation and light. Evangelistic preaching is preaching with a mission — an immediate and all-important mission — winning a verdict in favor of the Lord Jesus Christ." V. L. Stanfield offered the simpler definition: "the public proclamation of the gospel of Jesus Christ" with a view to gaining acceptance. Both definitions point to the same heart: a public, biblical, Spirit-empowered call to receive Christ.
blocks.es_reference: El evangelismo personal es la forma más común de proclamación del evangelio, pero no la única. Desde Pedro en Pentecostés hasta Whitefield en los campos y Spurgeon en el Tabernáculo, Dios ha usado la proclamación pública para reunir a miles. Faris Whitesell lo expresó con claridad: "La predicación evangelística es la predicación en su mejor forma. Es la predicación adaptada a los fines más altos del evangelio — apartando a los hombres del pecado y las tinieblas hacia la salvación y la luz. La predicación evangelística es la predicación con una misión — una misión inmediata y de suma importancia — ganar un veredicto a favor del Señor Jesucristo." V. L. Stanfield ofreció la definición más simple: "la proclamación pública del evangelio de Jesucristo" con miras a obtener aceptación. Ambas definiciones apuntan al mismo corazón: un llamado público, bíblico y empoderado por el Espíritu Santo a recibir a Cristo.

blocks.en: This unit examines what evangelistic preaching is, the New Testament terms for proclamation, the two things every evangelistic sermon must do, the presuppositions that make such preaching possible, the necessity of clarity and scriptural authority, dependence on the Spirit, the invitation, and the herald image that anchors the preacher's identity.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad examina qué es la predicación evangelística, los términos del Nuevo Testamento para la proclamación, las dos cosas que toda predicación evangelística debe hacer, las presuposiciones que la hacen posible, la necesidad de claridad y autoridad escritural, la dependencia del Espíritu Santo, la invitación, y la imagen del heraldo que ancla la identidad del predicador.

blocks.en: I. Six Definitions That Sharpen Our Vocabulary
blocks.es_reference: I. Seis Definiciones Que Afinan Nuestro Vocabulario

blocks.en: The English word "evangelism" carries a family of related terms. Distinguishing them prevents confusion.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra "evangelismo" lleva una familia de términos relacionados. Distinguirlos previene la confusión.

blocks.en: Evangel — the "good news" itself. The message about what God has done in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Evangelio — las "buenas nuevas" mismas. El mensaje sobre lo que Dios ha hecho en Cristo.

blocks.en: Evangelism — presenting that good news so that people receive it.
blocks.es_reference: Evangelismo — presentar esas buenas nuevas para que las personas las reciban.

blocks.en: Evangelist — one who carries the good news. Every pastor is in this sense an evangelist.
blocks.es_reference: Evangelista — uno que lleva las buenas nuevas. Todo pastor es en este sentido un evangelista.

blocks.en: Evangelistic — characterized by urgently propagating the good news.
blocks.es_reference: Evangelístico — caracterizado por propagar urgentemente las buenas nuevas.

blocks.en: Evangelical — one who endorses the work and emphasizes the receiving of the good news.
blocks.es_reference: Evangélico — uno que respalda la obra y enfatiza recibir las buenas nuevas.

blocks.en: Evangelistic Preaching — public proclamation of the gospel with the aim of conversion.
blocks.es_reference: Predicación Evangelística — proclamación pública del evangelio con el objetivo de la conversión.

blocks.en: One distinction is especially worth weighing: it is possible to be evangelical without being evangelistic. A church can hold orthodox doctrine, sing the right hymns, and never call a sinner to repent. The label is correct; the labor is missing. Evangelistic preaching exists to close that gap.
blocks.es_reference: Una distinción merece especial atención: es posible ser evangélico sin ser evangelístico. Una iglesia puede sostener doctrina ortodoxa, cantar los himnos correctos, y nunca llamar a un pecador al arrepentimiento. La etiqueta es correcta; la labor falta. La predicación evangelística existe para cerrar esa brecha.

blocks.en: II. The New Testament Terms for Preaching
blocks.es_reference: II. Los Términos del Nuevo Testamento para la Predicación

blocks.en: Warren Wiersbe identifies several Greek words behind "preaching" in the New Testament. Each adds a dimension.
blocks.es_reference: Warren Wiersbe identifica varias palabras griegas detrás de "predicación" en el Nuevo Testamento. Cada una añade una dimensión.

blocks.en: Euangelizomai — "to tell good news" (52 times). The fundamental verb of gospel proclamation.
blocks.es_reference: Euangelizomai — "anunciar buenas nuevas" (52 veces). El verbo fundamental de la proclamación del evangelio.

blocks.en: Kerussein — "to proclaim like a herald" (52 times). The related noun keryx (herald) and kerygma (proclamation) anchor the image.
blocks.es_reference: Kerussein — "proclamar como un heraldo" (52 veces). El sustantivo relacionado keryx (heraldo) y kerygma (proclamación) anclan la imagen.

blocks.en: Marturein — "to bear witness." John uses this word almost exclusively. Preaching from the heart.
blocks.es_reference: Marturein — "dar testimonio." Juan usa esta palabra casi exclusivamente. Predicar desde el corazón.

blocks.en: Lalein — "to talk" (6 times). Suggests a certain naturalness; preaching is conversation projected.
blocks.es_reference: Lalein — "hablar" (6 veces). Sugiere cierta naturalidad; la predicación es conversación proyectada.

blocks.en: Didaskein — "to teach" (95 times). The pulpit is also a classroom.
blocks.es_reference: Didaskein — "enseñar" (95 veces). El púlpito también es un aula.

blocks.en: The image that dominates is the keryx — the herald. In the Greek and Roman world the herald was the official announcer for the state. He had to have a clear voice and reliable character. He did not invent the message; he proclaimed it. John the Baptist is the first New Testament herald, announcing the coming Messiah. Every evangelistic preacher follows in that line: he carries another's message.
blocks.es_reference: La imagen que domina es el keryx — el heraldo. En el mundo griego y romano, el heraldo era el anunciador oficial del estado. Debía tener una voz clara y un carácter confiable. No inventaba el mensaje; lo proclamaba. Juan el Bautista es el primer heraldo del Nuevo Testamento, anunciando al Mesías venidero. Todo predicador evangelístico sigue en esa línea: lleva el mensaje de otro.

blocks.en: III. The Two Things Every Evangelistic Sermon Must Do
blocks.es_reference: III. Las Dos Cosas Que Todo Sermón Evangelístico Debe Hacer

blocks.en: Chevis Horne, in Dynamic Preaching, observes that evangelistic preaching is the preaching we must do first — if a man has a broken arm it must be set, and if he has a broken relationship with God it must be healed before anything else. Two things are essential.
blocks.es_reference: Chevis Horne, en Dynamic Preaching, observa que la predicación evangelística es la predicación que debemos hacer primero — si un hombre tiene un brazo roto, debe ser entablillado, y si tiene una relación rota con Dios, debe ser sanada antes que nada. Dos cosas son esenciales.

blocks.en: 1. The good news is announced. Evangelism means good news. To a lost person, it says, "Here is light." To one in chains, "You can be free." To the hungry, "Here is bread." To the blind, "You can see." To the dying, "You can live." Frederick Buechner adds that before it is good news, the gospel is bad news — a man is a sinner; that is tragedy. Against the bad news dawns the morning: God loves us anyway. That is comedy. It is too good to be true. That is fairy tale. Every evangelistic sermon must travel that arc — tragedy, sought, found — just as the lost sheep, the lost coin, and the lost son travel it in Luke 15.
blocks.es_reference: 1. Se anuncian las buenas nuevas. Evangelismo significa buenas nuevas. A una persona perdida le dice: "Aquí hay luz." A uno encadenado: "Puedes ser libre." Al hambriento: "Aquí hay pan." Al ciego: "Puedes ver." Al moribundo: "Puedes vivir." Frederick Buechner añade que antes de ser buenas nuevas, el evangelio es malas nuevas — el hombre es pecador; eso es tragedia. Contra las malas nuevas amanece la mañana: Dios nos ama de todos modos. Eso es comedia. Es demasiado bueno para ser verdad. Eso es cuento de hadas. Todo sermón evangelístico debe recorrer ese arco — tragedia, búsqueda, hallazgo — tal como la oveja perdida, la moneda perdida y el hijo perdido lo recorren en Lucas 15.

blocks.en: 2. Something is called for. Information is not enough. The sermon must call for repentance, faith, confession, and incorporation into the church. Peter at Pentecost closed his sermon with a direct command: "Repent, and let every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ" (Acts 2:38, NKJV). A sermon that announces the gospel but never asks for response has done half the work and left the soul at the threshold.
blocks.es_reference: 2. Se llama a algo. La información no es suficiente. El sermón debe llamar al arrepentimiento, la fe, la confesión y la incorporación a la iglesia. Pedro en Pentecostés cerró su sermón con un mandato directo: "Arrepentíos, y bautícese cada uno de vosotros en el nombre de Jesucristo" (Hechos 2:38, RVG). Un sermón que anuncia el evangelio pero nunca pide respuesta ha hecho la mitad de la obra y ha dejado al alma en el umbral.

blocks.en: IV. Nine Presuppositions That Make Evangelistic Preaching Possible
blocks.es_reference: IV. Nueve Presuposiciones Que Hacen Posible la Predicación Evangelística

blocks.en: Jay Brown distills the convictions on which evangelistic preaching rests. They are not optional theological flourishes; without them, the preacher will not preach evangelistically.
blocks.es_reference: Jay Brown destila las convicciones sobre las que descansa la predicación evangelística. No son adornos teológicos opcionales; sin ellas, el predicador no predicará evangelísticamente.

blocks.en: Brown's Presuppositions
blocks.es_reference: Las Presuposiciones de Brown

blocks.en: People without Christ are lost (John 3:18). They are without God and without hope.
blocks.es_reference: Las personas sin Cristo están perdidas (Juan 3:18). Están sin Dios y sin esperanza.

blocks.en: Preaching is God's chief means for saving the lost (Romans 10:14).
blocks.es_reference: La predicación es el medio principal de Dios para salvar al perdido (Romanos 10:14).

blocks.en: The pulpit is the preacher's greatest opportunity to evangelize — more people are reached at once than in any other engagement.
blocks.es_reference: El púlpito es la mayor oportunidad del predicador para evangelizar — alcanza a más personas a la vez que en cualquier otro encuentro.

blocks.en: Christ is God's only means of salvation (John 14:6). Not one among many.
blocks.es_reference: Cristo es el único medio de salvación de Dios (Juan 14:6). No uno entre muchos.

blocks.en: The Holy Spirit can produce life-changing experiences in the act of preaching.
blocks.es_reference: El Espíritu Santo puede producir experiencias transformadoras en el acto mismo de predicar.

blocks.en: The gospel is still the power of God unto salvation (Romans 1:16).
blocks.es_reference: El evangelio sigue siendo el poder de Dios para salvación (Romanos 1:16).

blocks.en: The mission of the church demands evangelistic preaching. Kerygma more than didache distinguishes the Christian faith.
blocks.es_reference: La misión de la iglesia exige predicación evangelística. El kerygma más que el didache distingue la fe cristiana.

blocks.en: Evangelistic preaching strengthens every other ministry of the church — attendance, giving, and spiritual growth all rise when souls are being saved.
blocks.es_reference: La predicación evangelística fortalece todos los demás ministerios de la iglesia — asistencia, ofrendas y crecimiento espiritual aumentan cuando se salvan almas.

blocks.en: Someone must do the reaping (John 4:35–38; Matthew 9:37–38).
blocks.es_reference: Alguien tiene que hacer la cosecha (Juan 4:35–38; Mateo 9:37–38).

blocks.en: G. Campbell Morgan stated the matter starkly: "No church ought to be allowed to exist that has not added to its membership by confession of faith. If a church is existing only by letters of transfer, it is time the doors were closed, and 'Ichabod, the glory of the Lord has departed' was inscribed across them." The presuppositions are not academic. They drive the preacher to the pulpit.
blocks.es_reference: G. Campbell Morgan declaró el asunto con franqueza: "Ninguna iglesia debería permitirse existir que no haya añadido a su membresía por confesión de fe. Si una iglesia existe solo por cartas de traslado, es hora de que se cierren las puertas y se inscriba sobre ellas: 'Icabod, la gloria del Señor se ha apartado.'" Las presuposiciones no son académicas. Llevan al predicador al púlpito.

blocks.en: V. The Centrality of the Gospel
blocks.es_reference: V. La Centralidad del Evangelio

blocks.en: Evangelistic preaching keeps the cross at the center. Paul declared, "For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified" (1 Corinthians 2:2, NKJV). Other topics may be addressed, but the death and resurrection of Christ are the sun around which they orbit. The CWT framework remains useful even in the pulpit: God's purpose (eternal life), our need (sin), God's provision (Christ's substitutionary death and resurrection), and the required response (repentance and faith). Sermons that fill the time with stories, humor, or moral advice while avoiding the offense of the cross have not preached the gospel, no matter how engaging they may be. The gospel itself is the power of God unto salvation (Romans 1:16, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: La predicación evangelística mantiene la cruz en el centro. Pablo declaró: "Pues nada me propuse saber entre vosotros, sino a Jesucristo, y a éste crucificado" (1 Corintios 2:2, RVG). Pueden tratarse otros temas, pero la muerte y la resurrección de Cristo son el sol alrededor del cual giran los demás. El marco del CWT sigue siendo útil incluso en el púlpito: el propósito de Dios (vida eterna), nuestra necesidad (pecado), la provisión de Dios (muerte sustitutiva y resurrección de Cristo) y la respuesta requerida (arrepentimiento y fe). Los sermones que llenan el tiempo con historias, humor o consejo moral mientras evitan la ofensa de la cruz no han predicado el evangelio, por muy atractivos que sean. El evangelio mismo es el poder de Dios para salvación (Romanos 1:16, RVG).

blocks.en: VI. Clarity and Scriptural Authority
blocks.es_reference: VI. Claridad y Autoridad Escritural

blocks.en: Public proclamation requires clear communication. Paul used a vivid analogy:
blocks.es_reference: La proclamación pública requiere comunicación clara. Pablo usó una analogía vívida:

blocks.en: "For if the trumpet makes an uncertain sound, who will prepare for battle?" (1 Corinthians 14:8, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Si la trompeta diere sonido incierto, ¿quién se preparará para la batalla?" (1 Corintios 14:8, RVG)

blocks.en: An uncertain trumpet confuses the soldiers. A vague sermon hinders response. The hearer must understand the message in order to respond to it. Clarity means using plain language, explaining biblical terms (grace, repentance, faith), organizing the message in a logical flow (problem → solution → response), and summarizing key points. The preacher should ask himself, "If a person who has never read the Bible heard this sermon, would he understand the gospel?" If not, the sermon needs revision.
blocks.es_reference: Una trompeta incierta confunde a los soldados. Un sermón vago dificulta la respuesta. El oyente debe entender el mensaje para responder a él. La claridad implica usar lenguaje sencillo, explicar términos bíblicos (gracia, arrepentimiento, fe), organizar el mensaje en un flujo lógico (problema → solución → respuesta) y resumir los puntos clave. El predicador debe preguntarse: "Si una persona que nunca ha leído la Biblia escuchara este sermón, ¿entendería el evangelio?" Si no, el sermón necesita revisión.

blocks.en: Clarity must be married to authority. Paul commanded Timothy, "Preach the word!" (2 Timothy 4:2, NKJV). The authority of the message does not come from the preacher's personality, education, or emotional intensity. It comes from the Word of God. The preacher is not a source of truth; he is a herald of truth already revealed. Therefore evangelistic preaching, however topical in form, must always be expository in foundation — explaining what the Bible actually says.
blocks.es_reference: La claridad debe casarse con la autoridad. Pablo ordenó a Timoteo: "Predica la palabra" (2 Timoteo 4:2, RVG). La autoridad del mensaje no proviene de la personalidad, la educación o la intensidad emocional del predicador. Proviene de la Palabra de Dios. El predicador no es una fuente de verdad; es un heraldo de la verdad ya revelada. Por tanto, la predicación evangelística, por más temática que sea en forma, debe ser siempre expositiva en su fundamento — explicando lo que la Biblia realmente dice.

blocks.en: VII. Dependence on the Holy Spirit
blocks.es_reference: VII. Dependencia del Espíritu Santo

blocks.en: As in all evangelism, preaching depends on the Spirit. Paul wrote, "And my speech and my preaching were not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power" (1 Corinthians 2:4, NKJV). The most carefully crafted sermon produces no spiritual fruit unless the Spirit applies it. The preacher must pray before, during, and after — relying on the Spirit for boldness, clarity, and the unseen work of conviction. He cannot manufacture conviction through emotional manipulation. Only the Spirit convicts.
blocks.es_reference: Como en todo evangelismo, la predicación depende del Espíritu Santo. Pablo escribió: "Ni mi palabra ni mi predicación fue con palabras persuasivas de humana sabiduría, sino con demostración del Espíritu y de poder" (1 Corintios 2:4, RVG). El sermón más cuidadosamente preparado no produce fruto espiritual a menos que el Espíritu Santo lo aplique. El predicador debe orar antes, durante y después — confiando en el Espíritu Santo para la valentía, la claridad y la obra invisible de la convicción. No puede fabricar convicción mediante manipulación emocional. Solo el Espíritu Santo convence.

blocks.en: Emotion may be present in evangelistic preaching, and it is not wrong — the gospel rightly moves the heart. But emotion must not replace truth. Responses based solely on emotion often lack lasting change. A person may weep at a moving story, walk an aisle, and yet not be born again. The preacher aims first at the mind — helping hearers understand the gospel — and lets the emotions follow from understanding.
blocks.es_reference: La emoción puede estar presente en la predicación evangelística, y no es incorrecta — el evangelio mueve correctamente el corazón. Pero la emoción no debe reemplazar la verdad. Las respuestas basadas únicamente en la emoción a menudo carecen de cambio duradero. Una persona puede llorar ante una historia conmovedora, caminar por un pasillo, y aún así no haber nacido de nuevo. El predicador apunta primero a la mente — ayudando a los oyentes a entender el evangelio — y deja que las emociones sigan al entendimiento.

blocks.en: VIII. The Invitation: Drawing the Net
blocks.es_reference: VIII. La Invitación: Recogiendo la Red

blocks.en: Evangelistic preaching calls for response. The invitation is not an emotional appendix to the sermon; it is the sermon's purpose. Peter's Pentecost sermon ended with a command, not a suggestion. Whitefield, Moody, and Graham all gave clear, urgent invitations. The shape of the invitation may vary — a private prayer, a raised hand, walking forward, a follow-up conversation — but the call must be made. The preacher should explain clearly what repentance and faith look like, name the moment of decision, and give an opportunity to respond. He must do this without manipulation. Pressure produces false converts. The Spirit produces true ones. The preacher's job is to make the way clear and the call urgent, and then to trust God for the response.
blocks.es_reference: La predicación evangelística llama a la respuesta. La invitación no es un apéndice emocional del sermón; es el propósito del sermón. El sermón de Pedro en Pentecostés terminó con un mandato, no una sugerencia. Whitefield, Moody y Graham dieron invitaciones claras y urgentes. La forma de la invitación puede variar — una oración privada, una mano levantada, caminar al frente, una conversación de seguimiento — pero el llamado debe hacerse. El predicador debe explicar claramente cómo se ve el arrepentimiento y la fe, nombrar el momento de decisión, y dar una oportunidad para responder. Debe hacerlo sin manipulación. La presión produce falsos conversos. El Espíritu Santo produce los verdaderos. El trabajo del predicador es hacer el camino claro y el llamado urgente, y luego confiar en Dios para la respuesta.

blocks.en: IX. The Herald: A Closing Image
blocks.es_reference: IX. El Heraldo: Una Imagen Final

blocks.en: Imagine the keryx in the public square. He does not invent the news; he announces it. He does not negotiate the king's decree; he proclaims it. He does not apologize for the message; he delivers it with urgency. His voice must be clear, his words accurate, and his demeanor faithful. If he whispers, the village does not hear. If he adds his own opinions, he distorts the message. If he apologizes, he undermines the king's authority. The evangelistic preacher is a herald for the King of Kings. Paul put it directly: "For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves your bondservants for Jesus' sake" (2 Corinthians 4:5, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Imagine al keryx en la plaza pública. No inventa las noticias; las anuncia. No negocia el decreto del rey; lo proclama. No se disculpa por el mensaje; lo entrega con urgencia. Su voz debe ser clara, sus palabras precisas y su actitud fiel. Si susurra, el pueblo no oye. Si añade sus propias opiniones, distorsiona el mensaje. Si se disculpa, socava la autoridad del rey. El predicador evangelístico es un heraldo del Rey de reyes. Pablo lo dijo directamente: "Porque no nos predicamos a nosotros mismos, sino a Jesucristo como Señor, y a nosotros como vuestros siervos por amor de Jesús" (2 Corintios 4:5, RVG).

blocks.en: Conclusion: Faithful Proclamation, Divine Power
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Proclamación Fiel, Poder Divino

blocks.en: Evangelistic preaching is a powerful means of proclaiming the gospel. When done faithfully, it communicates truth clearly and calls for response. Its effectiveness depends not on personality or method but on faithfulness to Scripture and dependence on God. The preacher must know the gospel, speak it clearly, rely on the Spirit, call for decision, and trust God for the increase. The pulpit is a sacred trust. Those who stand in it will give an account. Let them preach Christ crucified, risen, and coming again.
blocks.es_reference: La predicación evangelística es un medio poderoso de proclamar el evangelio. Cuando se hace fielmente, comunica la verdad con claridad y llama a la respuesta. Su eficacia no depende de la personalidad o el método, sino de la fidelidad a las Escrituras y la dependencia de Dios. El predicador debe conocer el evangelio, hablarlo con claridad, depender del Espíritu Santo, llamar a la decisión y confiar en Dios para el crecimiento. El púlpito es un encargo sagrado. Los que están de pie en él darán cuenta. Que prediquen a Cristo crucificado, resucitado y que vuelve.

blocks.en: Prayer: Lord, raise up heralds who will proclaim Your gospel faithfully. Give them clarity of mind, boldness of spirit, and humility of heart. Protect them from eloquence without truth, emotion without substance, and pressure without love. May every sermon be an arrow aimed at the heart, guided by Your Spirit, and effective for Your glory. In Jesus' name, Amen.
blocks.es_reference: Oración: Señor, levanta heraldos que proclamen Tu evangelio fielmente. Dales claridad de mente, valentía de espíritu y humildad de corazón. Protégelos de la elocuencia sin verdad, la emoción sin sustancia y la presión sin amor. Que cada sermón sea una flecha apuntada al corazón, guiada por Tu Espíritu, y eficaz para Tu gloria. En el nombre de Jesús, Amén.

mc.why: Whitesell: the immediate, all-important mission is 'winning a verdict in favor of the Lord Jesus Christ.'

mc.stem: Paul's resolve in 1 Corinthians 2:2 was to know nothing among the Corinthians except:
mc.why: 'For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.'

mc.stem: Paul's trumpet illustration (1 Corinthians 14:8) teaches that preaching must be:
mc.why: An uncertain trumpet confuses the soldiers — preaching must be clear so the hearer can respond.

mc.stem: Paul's charge to Timothy in 2 Timothy 4:2 was:
mc.why: 'Preach the word! Be ready in season and out of season.'

mc.stem: Paul's preaching, according to 1 Corinthians 2:4, was in demonstration of:
mc.why: Paul's preaching was 'in demonstration of the Spirit and of power' — not persuasive words of human wisdom.

mc.stem: The danger of emotionalism in evangelistic preaching is:
options: It produces shallow responses that lack lasting change
It cannot be used by God
mc.why: Emotion may attend the sermon but cannot replace truth — emotion-only responses often produce false converts.

mc.stem: The invitation in evangelistic preaching:
options: Must include a clear call to respond
Should be omitted to avoid pressure
mc.why: The invitation is the sermon's purpose — every evangelistic message must call clearly for response.

mc.stem: The town crier (keryx) illustrates that the preacher:
options: Is a herald of another's message
mc.why: The town crier announces what the king has decreed — like the preacher heralding what God has said.

mc.stem: The authority of evangelistic preaching comes from:
mc.why: Authority rests in Scripture — the preacher is a herald of truth already revealed, not its source.

mc.stem: Evangelistic preaching is effective ultimately because:
mc.why: The Spirit's application of the Word produces genuine conversion — apart from Him, no method or person can save.

fill.prompt: Faris Whitesell said evangelistic preaching is preaching with a mission: winning a ____ in favor of the Lord Jesus Christ.
It is possible to be ____ without being evangelistic: a church can hold orthodox doctrine and never call a sinner to repent.
The Greek verb didaskein means "to ____"; the pulpit is also a classroom.
The dominant image of preaching is the keryx, the ____, who was the official announcer for the state.
____ is the first New Testament herald, announcing the coming Messiah.
G. Campbell Morgan said a church existing only by letters of transfer should close its doors with "____, the glory of the Lord has departed" inscribed across them.
Paul kept the cross at the center: "For I determined not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ and Him ____" (1 Corinthians 2:2).
Because its authority comes from the Word of God, evangelistic preaching, however topical in form, must always be ____ in foundation.
The preacher cannot manufacture ____ through emotional manipulation; only the Spirit convicts.

sa.prompt: State Faris Whitesell's definition of evangelistic preaching and explain why he calls it 'preaching at its best.'
sa.model: Faris Whitesell defined evangelistic preaching as preaching that aims to bring the hearer to a decision for Christ — proclamation directed toward a verdict. He calls it preaching at its best because it does what all preaching ultimately exists to do: it confronts the hearer with the gospel and calls for a response, refusing to leave him merely informed. Preaching reaches its highest purpose when it seeks the soul's surrender to Christ.

sa.prompt: Compare and contrast Whitesell's and Stanfield's definitions of evangelistic preaching. What does each emphasize?
sa.model: Whitesell and Stanfield agree evangelistic preaching aims at a response but emphasize different things. Whitesell emphasizes the aim — preaching for a verdict, the decision the sermon seeks. Stanfield emphasizes the content and precision — what must be proclaimed for the preaching to be truly evangelistic, the clear gospel. Together they show evangelistic preaching needs both a clear gospel content and a deliberate call for decision.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between being 'evangelical' and being 'evangelistic.' Why is it possible to be one without the other?
sa.model: To be evangelical is to hold sound gospel doctrine — right belief about Christ and salvation. To be evangelistic is to actively proclaim that gospel to the lost. One can be evangelical without being evangelistic because a person or church may believe all the right things yet never share them. Correct doctrine that is never proclaimed saves no one; the evangelistic spirit turns sound belief into active witness.

sa.prompt: Identify the Greek terms 'euangelizomai' and 'kerussein.' Explain what each adds to our understanding of evangelistic preaching, and describe the herald (keryx) image.
sa.model: The Greek euangelizomai means to announce good news, stressing the joyful content of the message; kerussein means to herald or proclaim as a public crier, stressing the authoritative act of proclamation. The herald (keryx) image is of a messenger who announces a king's decree — he does not invent the message but delivers it faithfully and boldly. Together the terms show evangelistic preaching is the faithful, public proclamation of good news that is not the preacher's own.

sa.prompt: According to Chevis Horne, what are the two essential elements of every evangelistic sermon? Defend each as biblically required.
sa.model: According to Chevis Horne, every evangelistic sermon has two essential elements: an announcement of the good news of what God has done in Christ, and a call for response, inviting the hearer to act. Both are biblically required: the announcement is essential because there is no gospel without the message of Christ, and the call is essential because Scripture everywhere summons hearers to repent and believe. A sermon with only announcement informs; one with only a call manipulates. Both together preach the gospel rightly.

sa.prompt: Identify Jay Brown's first three presuppositions for evangelistic preaching and explain how each shapes the preacher's approach.
sa.model: Jay Brown's first three presuppositions for evangelistic preaching are that there are lost people present who need to be saved, that the gospel must actually be preached from the pulpit and not assumed, and that the preacher expects and aims for a response. Each shapes the preacher's approach: believing the lost are present keeps the gospel central every Sunday; refusing to assume the gospel makes him state it plainly; and expecting response leads him to call for decision rather than merely teach.

sa.prompt: G. Campbell Morgan wrote that 'no church ought to be allowed to exist that has not added to its membership by confession of faith.' Discuss the implications of this statement for the pastor's preaching ministry.
sa.model: G. Campbell Morgan said no church ought to exist that has not added to its membership by confession of faith. The implication for the pastor's preaching ministry is that his preaching must actually produce conversions, not merely instruct the already-converted. A church that never sees new believers come to faith and confess Christ has stopped being evangelistic. So the pastor must preach for decision, expecting his pulpit ministry to bear the fruit of genuine new converts joining the body.

sa.prompt: Explain why Paul's trumpet illustration (1 Corinthians 14:8) demands clarity in evangelistic preaching. What practical steps ensure that the hearer can understand the gospel?
sa.model: Paul's trumpet illustration in 1 Corinthians 14:8 says that if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, no one prepares for battle — an unclear message produces no response. This demands clarity in evangelistic preaching: the hearer cannot respond to a gospel he does not understand. Practical steps that ensure clarity include using plain language rather than jargon, defining terms like sin and grace, illustrating concretely, and stating the gospel and the call simply enough that an outsider could grasp and act on it.

sa.prompt: Discuss the role of the Holy Spirit in evangelistic preaching (1 Corinthians 2:4). Distinguish the preacher's role from the Spirit's, and explain why this dependence guards against manipulation.
sa.model: 1 Corinthians 2:4 shows Paul's preaching rested on the Spirit's power, not persuasive words. In evangelistic preaching the preacher's role is to proclaim the gospel clearly and faithfully; the Spirit's role is to convict and convert the heart. This dependence guards against manipulation because the preacher who trusts the Spirit has no need to engineer emotional pressure or manufacture decisions; he can preach the truth plainly and leave the results to God, who alone gives the new birth.

sa.prompt: Synthesize the unit: how do biblical content, presuppositions, clarity, Spirit-dependence, and the invitation come together to make evangelistic preaching faithful and effective?
sa.model: Faithful and effective evangelistic preaching combines several elements. Biblical content supplies the true gospel that must be proclaimed. Right presuppositions — that the lost are present and the gospel must be preached for a response — keep it evangelistic. Clarity ensures the hearer can understand. Spirit-dependence ensures it is God's power and not human pressure that converts. And the invitation calls the hearer to actually respond. Together, content, presuppositions, clarity, the Spirit, and the invitation make preaching both true to God and fruitful for souls.
